scope: Improve concrete CSS cascade fidelity without introducing rendering, decoding or full CSS evaluation.
implemented: Author important declarations survive later normal declarations and stylesheet important overrides inline normal; important declarations retain specificity/source-order precedence.
Important flags propagate to the already-supported margin/padding/border/background shorthand expansions.
Custom-property names remain case-sensitive in inline CSSOM, stylesheet declaration parsing and computed-style lookup.
Custom properties inherit across ordinary parents and shadow-host boundaries; document-version caching invalidates on mutation.
CSSOM custom-property writes trim outer whitespace consistently with reparsed attributes and the installed jsdom oracle.
Explicit inherit and inherited unset resolve from real parent declarations. Initial or noninherited unset values remain absent rather than inventing a catalog of browser defaults.

tests.focused_command: ASDF_NODEJS_VERSION=24.19.0 node --test test/css-cascade-fidelity.test.mjs test/inline-zero-length.test.mjs test/shadow.test.mjs test/shadow-features.test.mjs
tests.oracle_notes: Installed jsdom29.1.1 supports the ordinary important/inline and whitespace cases, but itself fails important-specificity and same-rule duplicate-important precedence. Those tests assert the CSS author-cascade ordering directly rather than using the oracle result.

performance.allocation_scope: Priority metadata is a lazily allocated Set only for declaration maps containing important values. Custom inheritance and keyword resolution execute only during getComputedStyle and remain memoized by document version.
performance.claim: No isolated throughput improvement or end-to-end suite speed claim; root performs integrated performance smoke.

remaining_limits: Real layout, raster rendering, media decoding/network loading/playback clocks remain outside a DOM test runtime. Existing synthetic geometry, virtual media APIs and canvas test backend are unchanged.
No var() substitution, fallback/cycle evaluation or registered custom-property semantics are added.
No complete initial-value catalog, CSS layers/revert, at-rule evaluation, pseudo-element style or state-dependent cascade is added.
Selector grammar and shorthand support remain partial; no selector parser/hot-path changes are made.
Shadow cascade retains its existing simplified specificity model; this change does not implement full encapsulation-context priority ordering.
